beats.say: You think the Cuban Missile Crisis was the only 1962 showdown-miss you missed the secret Berlin standoff.
On October 22, Kennedy warned the Soviet fleet in the Baltic, fearing a hidden naval clash.
But the real flashpoint was the U-2 overflights of the Soviet Black Sea base at Novorossiysk.
On November 1, a Soviet MiG scrambled, forcing the spy plane to ditch into the icy Black Sea.
The rescue mission, led by Admiral Sergey Gorshkov, used a disguised fishing trawler to retrieve the wreck.
U.S. intel hid the incident, fearing it would spark a naval arms race beyond the missiles.
Only weeks later, the Soviets deployed a secret anti-submarine fleet to the Caribbean, unseen by the world.
When the Cuban missiles fell, the hidden fleet was already on standby, ready to block any U.S. carrier.
This covert naval chess game kept the world from a second flash in 1962, a story erased from textbooks.
Imagine the seas trembling, not just the skies, as superpowers whispered war beneath waves.
